title: Massively Parallel RNA Assay with Immunoprecipitation for RNA-Protein Interactions
author: Lee, Rinn, et al.

steps.title: Design and prepare oligo pool
steps.instruction: Create a tiled oligonucleotide library with barcodes and adapters, synthesize the pool, and make stock and working solutions.

substeps.instruction: Define oligo architecture: 5′ adaptor (16 nt) – tile (157 nt) – molecular barcode (10 nt) – 3′ adaptor (17 nt). Use adaptor sequences 5′‑ACTGGCCGCTTCACTG‑3′ and 5′‑AGATCGGAAGAGCGTCG‑3′.
Select target RNAs (prefer longest isoform) and fragment each into overlapping 157‑nt tiles with 78‑nt overlap; include alternative‑exon tiles as needed.
Assign at least 15 unique 10‑nt barcodes per tile, ensuring uniqueness, no restriction sites (AgeI, NotI), no homopolymer runs ≥4 nt, GC ≤ 80 %, and minimum edit distance of 2.
Assemble the full pool of 5,835 oligonucleotides covering NORAD, HOTAIR, JPX, XIST, SRA1 and control RNU1‑1, each with 15 barcodes.
Order synthesis (e.g., Twist Bioscience). Dissolve received pool in TE buffer pH 8.0 (or 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0) to a stock concentration of 10 ng/µL.
Dilute the stock to a working concentration of 0.2 ng/µL for use in emulsion PCR.

steps.title: Culture and transfect HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Grow HEK293T cells and introduce the oligo‑pool plasmid using X‑tremeGENE HP.

substeps.instruction: Culture cells in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep + 1 % GlutaMAX.
Seed ~5 × 10⁶ cells per 15‑cm dish and incubate 1 day until 50‑70 % confluent.
Pre‑warm media (DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % GlutaMAX, no Pen/Strep), X‑tremeGENE HP reagent, and Opti‑MEM to 15‑25 °C.
Dilute 20 µg plasmid DNA in 2 mL Opti‑MEM.
Vortex X‑tremeGENE HP reagent briefly, then add 60 µL (3:1 reagent‑to‑DNA ratio) to the DNA/Opti‑MEM mixture.
Mix gently, incubate 15 min at 20‑25 °C.
Rinse cells twice with media lacking Pen/Strep, then add ~20 mL of the same media.
Add the transfection complex dropwise, incubate 6 h at 37 °C.
Replace with full growth media (DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % Pen/Strep + 1 % GlutaMAX) and return to incubator.
Incubate 24‑48 h; when cells reach 80‑100 % confluence, proceed to harvesting.

steps.title: Lyse cells, sonicate, and pre‑clear lysate
steps.instruction: Recover protein‑RNA complexes by lysis, sonication, filtration, and bead pre‑clearing.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑cool a Diagenode Bioruptor Pico to 4 °C.
Thaw cross‑linked cell pellet, resuspend in 1 mL cold RIPA buffer, rotate 10 min at 4 °C.
Sonicate: transfer 250 µL lysate to each 1.5 mL Bioruptor tube (4 tubes per 1 mL lysate); fill empty slots with water.
Run Easy Mode (10 s on/30 s off) for 3‑5 cycles at 4 °C.
Collect lysate, centrifuge 15,800 × g 10 min 4 °C, transfer supernatant to a new tube.
Add 1 mL cold fRIP buffer (final volume 2 mL) and filter through a 0.45 µm filter.
Prepare Protein G Dynabeads: 50 µL beads per sample, magnet‑pull, discard buffer, wash twice with 1 mL cold fRIP, resuspend in original volume.
Add 50 µL prepared beads to each lysate, rotate 30 min at 4 °C.
Magnet‑pull beads, collect cleared supernatant (pre‑cleared lysate).
Aliquot 25 µL as Input (optional second 25 µL for western blot).
Flash‑freeze lysates and Input aliquots; store at –80 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Reverse crosslink, isolate RNA, and DNase treat
steps.instruction: Reverse formaldehyde cross‑links, extract RNA, and remove contaminating DNA.

substeps.instruction: For Input samples, bring volume to 56 µL with nuclease‑free water; for IP samples, resuspend beads in 56 µL water and transfer entire mixture (beads included) to PCR tubes.
Add to each tube: 33 µL 3X Reverse Crosslinking Buffer, 10 µL 20 mg/mL Proteinase K, 1 µL 40 U/µL RNaseOUT.
Incubate 42 °C 1 h, then 55 °C 1 h.
Transfer contents to 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes (beads remain for IP).
Add 1 mL Trizol, mix, incubate 5 min at 20‑25 °C.
Add 200 µL chloroform, vortex ~15 s, incubate 3 min at 20‑25 °C.
Centrifuge 12,000 × g 15 min 4 °C; transfer aqueous phase.
Add 1 volume (~500 µL) 75 % ethanol, vortex.
Load 700 µL onto a Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini spin column, spin 8000 × g 15 s 4 °C; repeat until all sample loaded.
Wash with 700 µL Buffer RW1, spin 8000 × g 15 s 4 °C.
Wash twice with 500 µL Buffer RPE (first 15 s, second 2 min) at 8000 × g 4 °C.
Dry column 16,000 × g 2 min 4 °C.
Elute RNA with 30 µL RNase‑free water, spin 8000 × g 1 min 4 °C.
Quantify RNA using Qubit RNA HS Kit (Input ≈100 ng/µL expected).
Store RNA at –80 °C (≥1 month).
Aliquot 200 ng RNA into PCR tubes and adjust to 16 µL with water (if insufficient RNA, use the full 16 µL).
Prepare DNase master mix per sample: 2 µL 10X NEB DNase I Reaction Buffer + 2 µL NEB DNase I.
Add 4 µL master mix to each tube, incubate 37 °C 30 min.
Inactivate DNase at 75 °C 10 min.
Transfer 10 µL DNase‑treated RNA to new PCR tubes for downstream steps.

steps.title: Prime and reverse transcribe RNA to cDNA
steps.instruction: Generate cDNA from the purified RNA using random hexamer priming and SuperScript IV reverse transcriptase.

substeps.instruction: Prepare priming master mix per sample: 1 µL random hexamers (50 ng/µL), 1 µL 10 mM dNTP mix, 1 µL nuclease‑free water.
Add 3 µL priming mix to each 10 µL RNA tube, incubate 65 °C 5 min, then snap‑cool on ice.
Prepare RT master mix per sample: 4 µL 5X SuperScript IV Buffer, 1 µL SuperScript IV enzyme, 1 µL 100 mM DTT, 1 µL RNaseOUT (40 U/µL).
Add 7 µL RT master mix (final volume 20 µL).
Run thermal cycler program: 23 °C 10 min → 55 °C 10 min → 80 °C 10 min.
Store resulting cDNA at –20 °C (≥1 month).

description: This protocol details a step-by-step workflow that includes oligonucleotide design for tiling RNA with or without systematic mutations, large-scale oligonucleotide cloning, mammalian cell transfection, formaldehyde crosslinking, immunoprecipitation of RNA-protein complexes, sequencing library preparation, and a complete computational pipeline for downstream analysis. For demonstration of this protocol, we applied it to long noncoding RNA (lncRNA)’s interaction with the RNA-binding protein Pumilio (PUM2) and examined its established binding motif, the Pumilio Response Element (PRE).2,3 A pooled oligonucleotide library tiling five lncRNAs (NORAD, HOTAIR, JPX, XIST, and SRA1) and a control RNA (RNU1-1), with 15 barcodes assigned to each tile, was synthesized comprising 5,835 oligonucleotides. Then, the pool was transfected to HEK293T cells, immunoprecipitated with PUM2, and the PUM2-binding RNA were purified and subjected to high-throughput sequencing. Subsequent computational analysis successfully recovered the PRE motif from the sequencing results, demonstrating the applicability of the approach. Note: In addition to lncRNA, this protocol can also be adapted to study mRNA–protein interaction studies without changes to the core workflow. For studies focused on post-transcriptional regulation, tiling can be restricted to specific regions of interest, such as the 5′ UTR or 3′ UTR, rather than the full transcript; this targeted approach is more cost-effective and better suited for identifying regulatory elements, as UTRs are well-established sites of RBP interaction. Alternatively, if the goal is to survey the entire transcript without prior assumptions about binding location, full-length tiling can be considered as described here. In this protocol, expressed tiles are driven by a minimal CMV promoter and polyadenylated via an SV40 poly(A) signal, enabling analysis of RNA-protein interactions, particularly in the cytoplasmic context.
